claim: Girona Cathedral cultural visit ticket is €5 (students/65+ €3, under 7 free, audioguide included); open Apr-Oct 10:00-20:00 and Nov-Mar 10:00-19:00, with free Sunday entry to Treasury and Cloister
quote: Cultural visit €5 (includes audioguide); students/65+: €3; under 7: free. April-October: 10:00 to 20:00; November-March: 10:00 to 19:00. Free Sundays (Treasury & Cloister 10:00-14:00)

claim: Girona Cathedral has the widest Gothic nave in the world at 22.98 m, second-widest nave of any ecclesiastical style after St Peter's in Rome; the single Gothic nave was begun by Guillem Bofill and Antoni Canet in 1416
quote: a large Gothic nave—the widest Gothic nave in the world—at 22.98 m... surpassed only by St. Peter's Basilica in Rome. Guillem Bofill and Antoni Canet started the project in 1416

claim: Girona Cathedral's Baroque main facade (begun 1606) sits atop ninety stone steps, with the staircase completed in 1607
quote: a Baroque facade at the top of ninety stone steps... The church has a Baroque main façade (begun in 1606)... preceded by a large staircase completed in 1607

claim: The Cathedral Treasury houses the Tapestry of Creation (Tapis de la Creació, c. 11th-12th century), a jewel of Catalan Romanesque art
quote: the Tapis de la Creació (Tapestry of the Creation, c. XI-XII), described as one of the jewels of Romanesque art in Catalonia

claim: Basilica of Sant Feliu opens Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00, Sun/holidays 13:00-18:00; combined Cathedral + Sant Feliu ticket is €7.50 (€5 reduced); it holds eight 4th-century pagan and early-Christian sarcophagi and a 14th-century Recumbent Christ by Aloi de Montbrai
quote: Cathedral + Basilica of Sant Feliu: €7.50 / €5.00 / €1.50... eight pagan and early Christian sarcophagi (4th century)... Recumbent Christ (14th century) by the sculptor Aloi de Montbrai... Mon to Sat 10AM-6PM; Sundays and bank holidays 1PM-6PM

claim: Museum of Jewish History admission is €6 (€3 reduced; under 16 free; free first Sunday of each month); open Sep-Jun Tue-Sat 10:00-18:00, Mon/Sun/holidays 10:00-14:00, with extended summer hours in Jul-Aug
quote: General Admission: €6. Reduced Rate: €3... Free Entry: Children under 16... Free admission on the first Sunday of every month. September to June: Tuesday to Saturday from 10 am to 6 pm; Monday, Sunday and bank holidays from 10 am to 2 pm

claim: The Museum of Jewish History occupies the former Call within El Call and uses eleven thematic galleries to cover medieval Catalan Jewish life, including the aljama, synagogues, cemeteries and the Inquisition
quote: eleven galleries organized around thematic areas covering medieval Jewish life in Catalonia... The main aim of the Museum is to preserve and reflect the history of the Jewish communities of Catalonia

claim: Girona's Call was one of the most important Jewish communities in the medieval West and is the best-preserved Jewish quarter in Europe, home to the community for some six centuries
quote: one of the most important Jewish communities in the West and is currently the best preserved call in Europe. The Jewish community lived here 6 centuries

claim: Girona's Arab Baths charge €3 general admission (€2 over-65, €1 students/under-16/unemployed) and open Mon-Sat 10:00-18:00, Sun/holidays 10:00-14:00
quote: General Admission Price: 3 euros per person. Reduced Price: 2 euros per person for those over 65... 1 euro per person... Monday through Saturday: 10 am to 6 pm; Sundays and bank holidays: 10 am to 2 pm

claim: Girona's Arab Baths are a 12th-century Romanesque bathhouse modelled on Roman and Moorish baths despite the name
Sant Pere de Galligants is a Romanesque monastery (begun late 10th century, completed 12th century) now housing the Girona branch of the Archaeology Museum of Catalonia
quote: located in the Sant Pere de Galligants Monastery in the historic centre of the city... a Romanesque religious building whose construction began at the end of the 10th century and was completed in the 12th century

claim: Girona's medieval city walls (Passeig de la Muralla) are freely walkable along the old town, offering elevated views over the city and cathedral
quote: The Walls | Tourism | Girona City Council

claim: Girona stood in for Braavos, King's Landing and Oldtown in Game of Thrones Season 6: the Cathedral steps were the Great Sept of Baelor (Jaime vs the High Sparrow), the Jewish Quarter and Sant Martí Sacosta steps were Braavos (Arya/the Waif), Sant Pere de Galligants was Oldtown's Citadel, and the Arab Baths and a nearby bridge featured in Arya's chase
quote: Cathedral Steps: exterior for the Great Sept of Baelor... Jewish Quarter Streets depicted the city of Braavos where Arya Stark's storyline unfolded... Sant Pere de Galligants Monastery represented the citadel in Oldtown... Arab Baths used as a location where Arya is trying to hide while fleeing from the waif. All locations filmed during Season 6
